briefs.claim_en: COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips to track vaccinated individuals.
briefs.brief_en: Multiple fact-checking organizations and health authorities, including Tempo.co, FactCheck.org, AFP Fact Check, the CDC, and the Indonesian Ministry of Health, consistently state that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips. Experts explain that microchips are too large to be injected with vaccine needles and require power and an antenna to function, which is not present in vaccines. Some sources suggest the conspiracy theory may stem from misinterpretations of digital vaccine records or the existence of subdermal microchips developed by a Swedish company in December 2021 for storing vaccination data, which are separate from the vaccines themselves and cannot track location. Claims linking Bill Gates to microchip implants in vaccines have also been debunked.
